Requirement: Applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors acting on the org's behalf
Covers third-party AI tools (web chat, browser extensions, IDE plugins, AI features inside SaaS), model APIs, and internally hosted/fine-tuned models
A SaaS vendor switching on an AI feature counts as a new tool, not a product update
Use only tools on the approved register, regardless of whether the tool is free or personal
[Enterprise chat assistant] | Tier: Enterprise (SSO, no training on inputs) | Max classification: Confidential | Uses: general drafting, analysis, code | Contract: DPA, retention, no-train checked
[Coding assistant] | Tier: Enterprise | Max classification: Internal + source code | Uses: code completion/review in approved repos | Contract: checked
[Self-hosted model] | Tier: Internal | Max classification: Restricted (per model card) | Uses: per model card intended use
Consumer/personal accounts of any tool | Not approved | Max classification: Public only | Uses: nothing involving org data
New tool requests go through [process/form]; security review covers retention, training-on-inputs, residency, SSO, audit logging, sub-processors
Enterprise and consumer tiers of the same product are different tools - approval is for the contract, not the brand
If you wouldn't email it to the vendor, don't paste it into their model
Public: consumer/unapproved = Yes; approved enterprise = Yes; internally hosted = Yes
Internal: consumer/unapproved = No; approved enterprise = Yes; internally hosted = Yes
Confidential (customer data, financials, unreleased plans, source code): consumer/unapproved = No; approved enterprise = Only if register allows; internally hosted = If deployment approved
Restricted (credentials, secrets, PHI, PCI, government IDs): consumer/unapproved = No; approved enterprise = No; internally hosted = No unless explicitly approved per deployment
Passwords, API keys, tokens, private keys, connection strings - including in pasted logs, configs, or stack traces
Customer/employee personal data beyond what the approved use strictly needs
Data contractually or legally barred from third-party sharing (check customer contracts and NDAs)
Material under legal hold or privilege
Attachments, screenshots, voice, and Drive/email integrations count as prompts; connecting a mailbox or file store grants access to everything that account can read
Drafting/editing, summarizing shareable documents, brainstorming, code assistance, research starting points, translation, analysis on appropriately classified data (approved tools only)
Making or fully automating significant decisions about people (hiring, firing, ratings, credit, individual pricing, eligibility) without documented human review and Legal sign-off
Impersonating a real person, or presenting content as human-written where disclosure is required
Circumventing tool safety controls or org guardrails outside an authorized red-team engagement
Using AI to violate any existing policy (harassment, discrimination, IP, export control, security) - 'the model wrote it' is not an exception
Uploading third-party copyrighted/licensed material in ways the license doesn't permit
The person who uses AI output is accountable for it
Verify facts, citations, numbers, and legal/medical/financial claims against a primary source
Review AI code like a stranger's PR: hardcoded secrets, injection flaws, insecure defaults, invented/typosquatted packages, licensing of reproduced snippets; normal code review and CI scanning apply
Human review of customer-facing content before sending or publishing
Read commands and scripts before running, especially anything touching production, deleting data, or changing permissions
Disclose AI involvement where readers would reasonably expect it and wherever law or contract requires (e.g. customer-facing chatbots identify as AI; [jurisdiction-specific e.g. EU AI Act])
Don't present AI-generated work as solely your own where authorship matters (publications, legal filings, academic work, formal reports)
AI-generated images/audio/video depicting real people require [Legal/Comms] approval
Agents/automations with write access to org systems need security review before go-live
Run agents under a scoped service identity, not a personal account
Human approval step for irreversible or external-facing actions
MCP servers, plugins, and extensions follow the same approval process as tools
Treat all content the model reads as potentially carrying instructions; agents shouldn't hold more privilege than their least-trusted input
API keys in a secrets manager, per-environment, rotated; never in code, notebooks, or client-side bundles
Use org-managed accounts/billing for model APIs - no personal keys on company work
Complete the pre-deployment checklist and a model card before hosting or exposing a model
Download open-weight models only from official sources and scan before loading - model files can execute code
Spending limits and usage alerts set on every API account
Pasted restricted/confidential data into an unapproved tool (early reporting enables deletion requests; not a disciplinary trap)
Model output leaks other users' or org data
An agent or integration took an unintended action
Jailbreak or guardrail bypass found in an org-deployed model
A team is using an unapproved AI tool on org data
Complete [AI usage training] before access to approved tools; refresh annually
Annual policy acknowledgment tracked by [HR/GRC]
Violations handled under existing [acceptable use/disciplinary] policy
